applicable_when: The kernel is a pure transpose (layout permutation) over a 15360x9 element space. The current tile configuration (XBLOCK=128, YBLOCK=8) is badly mismatched: xnumel=9 means 119 of 128 X-threads are masked out every CTA — 93% thread waste in the X dimension. The resulting grid of 1920 CTAs across 132 SMs yields only 0.91 waves, leaving ~half the SMs idle during the tail wave. Achieved occupancy is 62.3% vs 100% theoretical. Switching to XBLOCK=1 (or a small power-of-2 <= 16) and scaling YBLOCK up (e.g. 64-256) will: (a) eliminate masked-thread waste, (b) increase the number of active warps per SM, (c) improve memory coalescing on the Y dimension, and (d) allow more waves to fill the GPU. @triton.autotune explores the best combination automatically.

applicable_when: The kernel performs a transpose/permutation of a (32,480,3,3) tensor. With XBLOCK=128 and xnumel=9, the X-dimension tile is massively over-provisioned (128 threads for 9 elements = 86% waste). YBLOCK=8 is tiny, producing 1920 blocks on 132 SMs = 0.91 waves — barely one full wave. Increasing YBLOCK (e.g. to 64) reduces the grid to 240 blocks (1.82 waves/SM), each block doing far more useful work per launch, improving L1 cache reuse and warp efficiency. Simultaneously, XBLOCK should be reduced to 16 (covering xnumel=9 with minimal padding) to avoid wasting threads. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the best tile configuration automatically.
